meta.thesis: Boba Tea Protein turns the boba occasion into a protein occasion — starting inside the 1,269 Texas shops where customers already buy it.
meta.variant_angle: channel-gap: boba shops + protein RTD intersection

business_problem: Boba Tea Protein sells 100% direct-to-consumer online, but the boba occasion happens inside shops: the US has 11,162 boba shops and Texas alone has 1,269 — where this brand has zero presence. It is also asking consumers to build a new 'protein boba' habit with no retail or foodservice touchpoints.

objectives.text: Drive 1,500 new DTC orders during the 45-day window
Grow the owned audience by 6,000 email/SMS subscribers and 12,000 site sessions
Generate 3.5M campaign impressions and 400K engagements across TikTok, Instagram, and creator content

segments.name: Savannah, 22 — the Gen-Z Gym-Goer & Boba Regular
segments.demographic: 18-27, urban and suburban Texas, college students and early-career, female-skewing fitness audience
segments.geographic: Texas metros with high boba density — Dallas/Fort Worth, Austin, Houston, San Antonio
segments.psychographic: Tracks macros, values 'real ingredients,' sees boba as a treat she wants to make healthier; follows fitness and food creators on TikTok
segments.behavioral: Buys boba weekly at shops; buys protein powder monthly; discovers brands on TikTok and through friends
segments.media: TikTok (daily), Instagram Reels, YouTube, group chats; low email engagement, high SMS response

segments.name: Marcus, 31 — the New Year Resolver
segments.demographic: 28-40, suburban Texas, household income $60K+, parents and professionals
segments.psychographic: January resolution-driven: wants to cut sugar without giving up favorite drinks; pragmatic, research-driven buyer
segments.behavioral: Buys protein shakes and functional beverages; searches Amazon and Google; rarely visits boba shops
segments.media: Google search, Amazon, Instagram, podcasts; email newsletters, not TikTok

methods.recruitment: Agency desk audit of Guardian review + brand sites

programs.name: Sip at the Shop
programs.mechanic: Proposed sampling partnership with 20 independent Texas boba shops: free sample cups of Protein Matcha, counter cards with QR code, and a $5-off-first-order code per shop. Shop owners get 15% wholesale margin on referred sales.

programs.name: #MyProteinBoba Challenge
programs.mechanic: UGC challenge: customers post a video of their protein boba creation with #MyProteinBoba and @bobateaprotein; weekly winners get a free tub. All posts must include #ad disclosure per FTC rules.

programs.name: New Year Reset Creator Seeding
programs.mechanic: Seed 8 fitness and food micro-creators (5K-50K followers) in Texas with product + unique discount codes; each posts one honest 'protein boba vs regular boba' video in weeks 1-3.

programs.name: Founder's Protein Lab
programs.mechanic: Founder Neil Hoang (personal trainer, lost 60 lbs) hosts a weekly 'Protein Lab' email + TikTok series: one flavor, its macros, and a 60-second recipe. Sent to the owned email/SMS list with a shop-code tie-in.

programs.name: Valentine's Sip Kit
programs.mechanic: Limited 'Sip Kit' gift bundle (tub + printed recipe card + sticker pack) promoted in weeks 5-6 to gift buyers; email push plus paid social to the P2 segment.

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: Boba Tea Protein sells 100% online, but the boba occasion happens inside shops - 11,162 US shops and 1,269 in Texas where the brand has zero presence [S2][S5].

Business opportunity: protein RTD sales jumped 13% to $7.6B in 2025 while bubble tea grows ~11% a year - 'protein boba' is an unclaimed intersection, and The Guardian just named the brand best overall [S1][S4][S6].
Solution: 'Sip Stronger' puts protein boba inside Texas boba shops for sampling, then converts that trial into DTC orders through a UGC challenge and creator seeding [O1].
45-day goal: 1,500 new orders and 6,000 new email/SMS subscribers [O1][O2].

visual.desc: Four boxes: Problem / Business opportunity / Solution / 45-day goal

slides.notes: Open with the shop statistic: the customer buys boba in a shop six days a week, but this brand only exists on a website. That is the structural problem we are solving.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Grass-fed whey protein powder in authentic boba flavors: matcha, Vietnamese coffee, taro, jasmine, strawberry [S5].
Real tea ingredients, monk fruit sweetener, zero sugar added; third-party tested in an NSF(GMP)-certified facility [S5].
Priced $44.99-$59.99 per tub [S5]; each tub makes ~20 protein boba drinks [A1].
Named 'best overall' in The Guardian's Nov 2025 taste test of 14 protein boba drinks [S6].

visual.desc: Flat-lay of 4 flavor tubs with matcha latte art and boba pearls

slides.notes: Emphasize the proof: a national newspaper taste test picked this brand first. That is earned credibility we can amplify, not create.

slides.title: The Company & Its Position
bullets: Dallas-based, founded by personal trainer Neil Hoang after his own 60-lb weight-loss journey [S5][S7].
12 employees, headcount up 140% year over year - a brand in hypergrowth [S7].
Sells 100% DTC online today - no retail, no foodservice, no shop presence [S5].
Position: premium 'real ingredient' protein boba at ~$50, between budget powders and cafe drinks [S5][S6].

visual.desc: Positioning map: x = price, y = 'boba authenticity'; brand sits top-right, competitors clustered lower-left

slides.notes: The company is exactly the kind of client an agency wants: growing fast, real product proof, and a clear channel gap to fix. We are proposing the fix.

slides.title: Research Method & Results
bullets: Secondary research (complete): Mordor Intelligence, IBISWorld, SPINS/NBJ via New Hope, Smartscrapers store data, Guardian taste test [S1][S2][S3][S4][S6].
Key results: 11,162 US boba shops, Texas #2 at 1,269 [S2]; protein RTDs +13% to $7.6B [S4]; US bubble tea market $511M growing to $857M by 2031 [S1].
Primary research (in field): 8-question survey of 16-34 boba/protein buyers + 3-5 customer interviews; results load into slides 10 and 17 before submission [R-pending].

Environmental scan: Gen-Z boba culture is mainstream (Gong Cha cites TikTok as its growth engine) [S2]; sugar scrutiny pushes 'better-for-you' formats [S1]; protein is the top-selling supplement focus [S4].

visual.desc: Methods table: 4 methods with n/status, plus bar chart of key market stats

slides.notes: Be honest that primary fieldwork is in progress - then show the secondary base is already deep enough to drive decisions.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: Finding: the boba purchase happens in shops, not online [S2] -> therefore we will sample inside 20 Texas boba shops (G1) instead of spending the whole budget on ads.
Finding: protein RTD is the fastest-growing supplement format and 'protein boba' has no dominant brand [S4][S6] -> therefore the campaign owns the phrase 'protein boba' with #MyProteinBoba (G2).
Finding: Texas is the #2 boba state and the brand is headquartered in Dallas [S2][S7] -> therefore the hero push is Texas-first, starting in DFW shops.
Finding: The Guardian's taste test is fresh third-party proof [S6] -> therefore PR re-amplifies the 'best overall' result instead of inventing claims.
Finding (pending survey): channel and price-preference data will re-weight paid media vs. shop spend in week 1 [R-pending].

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Big idea 'Sip Stronger': turn the weekly boba run into a protein upgrade - try it at the shop, post it, sip it stronger.
IMC mix: Paid (TikTok/Meta) + Earned (Guardian proof, PR) + Shared (UGC challenge) + Owned (email/SMS, shop codes, POS cards).
Push-pull: shops get sampling and margin (push); consumers get creator proof and a challenge (pull); both point to the same offer: five dollars off the first order [O1].
Ownable element competitors cannot copy: founder Neil Hoang's trainer story plus the only 'best overall' protein-boba taste-test win [S5][S6].

visual.desc: Key visual: split image - regular boba cup vs. Protein Matcha tub, 'Sip Stronger' lockup

slides.notes: Theme check: 'Sip Stronger' appears on every activity slide. That consistency is what makes a campaign feel like one idea, not five tactics.

slides.title: 45-Day Schedule
bullets: Weeks 1-2 (Jan 5-18): Sip Stronger tease + seed - creator videos drop, shop sampling begins in DFW, email/SMS capture starts [O3].
Weeks 3-4 (Jan 19-Feb 1): challenge launch - #MyProteinBoba goes live under the Sip Stronger banner, weekly prizes, retargeting begins [O1][O3].
Weeks 5-6 (Feb 2-15): convert - Valentine's Sip Kit push to gift buyers, last-chance challenge reminder [O1][O2].
Week 7 (Feb 16-18): close - results recap to the list, winner announcement, retention offer [O2].

slides.title: Program 1: Sip at the Shop
bullets: Sip Stronger goes physical: 20 independent Texas boba shops sample Protein Matcha for 7 weeks [O1][O2].
Mechanic: free 2-oz sample cup + counter card with shop-specific QR code + a five-dollar-off-first-order offer.
Why it works: 1,269 Texas shops already own the boba occasion [S2]; we rent their foot traffic instead of buying cold traffic.
Measurement: per-shop QR codes attribute every order; target 25% of campaign orders from shop codes [A7].

slides.title: Program 2: #MyProteinBoba Challenge
bullets: Sip Stronger becomes a hashtag: customers film their protein boba creation, post with #MyProteinBoba, win a tub weekly [O1][O3].
Mechanic: 5 weekly winners; all entrants entered via site form that captures email/SMS consent (TCPA-compliant opt-in) [O2].
Seeding: challenge goes live week 3 after creator videos (G3) model the format - 'protein boba vs. regular boba' taste test.
Target: 300 UGC posts; every post is a trackable asset for paid whitelisting [O3].

slides.notes: The challenge is the ownable twist: it only works because the product makes real boba-style drinks at home. A whey brand cannot copy it.

Named decision-maker: Neil's credibility is the reason-to-believe; his story is the creative asset [S5].
8 Texas micro-creators (5K-50K) seed the message weeks 1-3 with unique discount codes for attribution [O3].

slides.title: Proposed Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total campaign budget: $20,000 across media, creators, sampling, production, tools, PR, and 10% contingency [A4][A6][A7][A8][A9][A10][A11][A12].
Funnel math: 3.5M impressions x 1.2% CTR = 42K clicks x 4% conversion = 1,680 orders x $50 AOV = $84K revenue [A1][A4].
Gross profit at 62% margin = $52K; profit-based ROI = 160%; ROAS = 6.0x on $14K ad spend [A2].
Break-even = 645 orders; base case 1,680, conservative case (50%) 840 orders still clears break-even [O1].
CAC = $11.90 base / $23.81 conservative vs. $50 AOV - healthy payback inside the campaign window [A1][A2].

visual.desc: Line-item budget table + funnel math + base/conservative case table

slides.notes: Lead with break-even: the campaign pays for itself at 645 orders, and our conservative case is 840. That is a financial answer, not a hope.

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1 orders: tracked via per-program promo codes + Shopify; target 1,500; checked weekly [O1].
O2 list growth: Klaviyo/SMS dashboard; target +6,000 subscribers and 12,000 UTM sessions [O2].
O3 reach: TikTok/Meta Ads Manager + hashtag tracking; target 3.5M impressions, 400K engagements, 300 UGC posts [O3].
Optimization trigger: if TikTok CTR < 0.8% by day 10, shift 20% of paid budget to Meta; if shop-code redemptions < 5% by week 3, add a second sampling wave [A4].
Post-campaign: 30-day holdout read on repeat purchase to prove LTV, not just launch sales [A3].

visual.desc: KPI table: objective -> KPI -> baseline -> target -> tool -> cadence

slides.notes: Every metric has a baseline plan, a target, a tool, and a cadence. That is the difference between reporting and measurement.

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Mission metric: every tub makes ~20 protein boba drinks - the campaign targets 1,500 orders = ~30,000 'better boba' moments [A1][O1].
Founder thesis: 'make the healthiest boba tea in the most authentic way possible' - Sip Stronger brings that promise to the counter where boba is actually bought [S5].
Projected result: $84K attributed revenue on a $20K budget, 840+ orders even in the conservative case [O1].
The lasting asset: 6,000 owned subscribers and a reusable shop-partner playbook for the next launch [O2].
